items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I accepted to replace Billy until he came out of the hospital... With our trio of piano, bass and trumpet, we took care of the dancing.

ctx.x: One day, Al Hall came to my house and asked me if I would like to replace a guitarist named Billy Moore who was sick in a hospital. My brother(who was a tailor) and I were sharing a three-roomed furnished apartment on 161st Street and I had not seen Al for quite some time. He told me that he was working at the Cafe Society Uptown with Billy Moore and a pianist.

I was surprised because Teddy Wilson had told me two years before that Barney Josephson had said that he never wanted Al and myself in his place again. I accepted to replace Billy until he came out of the hospital and that night I met the pianist. His name was Ellis Larkins, was from Baltimore and had been studying at Julliard music college on a scholarship he had won in his home town.

Teddy Wilson was still in the club with Joe Thomas on trumpet John Williams, bass, and Sid Catlett, drums. I don't remember who was playing sax, but Benny Morton was still with the band. The show had Hazel Scott, the Golden Gate Quartet, two sisters who danced East Indian dances named the Craft Sisters, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons, the two boogie woogie pianists. With our trio of piano, bass and trumpet, we took care of the dancing. It was the first time that I played with only a piano and bass. Our salary was…
